original_title: Marvel's Wolverine Developer Nerfs Scent Trails and Audio Sense Indicators After 'Fart Gas' Backlash
summary_en: Insomniac Games has responded to player feedback regarding the scent trail mechanic in Marvel's Wolverine, implementing adjustments after it drew comparisons to 'fart gas.' The developer aims to refine the visual indicator for Logan's tracking abilities.

en.title: Marvel's Wolverine: Insomniac Tweaks 'Fart Gas' Trail After Fan Backlash
en.summary: Insomniac Games has responded to player feedback regarding the scent trail mechanic in Marvel's Wolverine, implementing adjustments after it drew comparisons to 'fart gas.' The developer aims to refine the visual indicator for Logan's tracking abilities.
en.body:
## The Scent of Controversy

Even before **Marvel's Wolverine** officially hit store shelves, a particular visual element had already sparked considerable online debate: the scent trail players follow to track targets. This distinctive visual effect, which appears behind characters or clues, quickly earned the informal moniker "fart gas" from some corners of the internet, most notably drawing attention from journalists like Gene Park. The ensuing discussion saw some players confused about whether this navigational aid could be toggled off, especially given the game's robust accessibility options.

Insomniac Games has since clarified the nature of this mechanic. Community and marketing director James Stevenson explained that the scent trail is not a constant visual overlay but rather a representation of Logan's canon mutant super senses and elite tracking abilities. It appears only during specific story or mission moments when Logan is actively tracking a particular scent or sound – be it a person, a clue, or even a collectible. This explanation aims to ground the visual in the established lore of the character, emphasizing its functional role within the narrative.

## Community Reactions and Developer Response

The "fart gas" nickname, while perhaps unflattering, underscored a community desire for control over visual elements that might feel intrusive or detract from the immersive experience. Some players drew parallels to the yellow paint guides seen in previous games like **Final Fantasy**, suggesting that overly explicit markers could diminish the sense of skill involved in tracking. While the scent trail is tied to Logan's abilities, the community's vocalization prompted Insomniac to revisit its implementation. Following the feedback, an update has been released that aims to nerf these scent trails and audio sense indicators, striking a balance between lore accuracy and player preference.

## What's Next

Insomniac Games continues to refine **Marvel's Wolverine** post-launch, demonstrating a commitment to player feedback. Further updates may address other gameplay elements as the studio gathers more player data and reactions. The exact details of the nerf to the scent trails and audio indicators have not been fully elaborated upon, but the intention is to make them less obtrusive while still serving their narrative purpose.

content_raw: Insomniac has released an update for Marvel’s Wolverine that nerfs the “fart gas” that had become such a talking point even before the game’s release. The debate around this was rekindled following the publication of Marvel’s Wolverine reviews earlier this month, with The Washington Post journalist Gene Park calling the scent trail “fart gas” because of the way it appears behind characters Logan follows. Jean Grey’s fart gas trail is NOT part of the navigation assist option. i turned it on and there’s another green line that tells you where to go. mission waypoint (yellow marker) is on as well and THAT can be turned off. 2nd pic i turn off the options and the gas stays. it seems… pic.twitter.com/cKs9uTPSG0 — Gene Park (@GenePark) September 10, 2026 There was some confusion online about the ability to turn this feature off via accessibility options. Insomniac’s official list of accessibility options for Wolverine includes a “Chase Assist,” which lets you toggle reduced movement speed for targets during chase sequences, but it does not turn off the trail. Other navigation toggles do not turn off the scent trail either. Ahead of Wolverine’s release, Insomniac’s director of community and marketing, James Stevenson, took to social media to explain that Logan's scent trail is baked into the way the mutant's powers work. “The scent trail isn’t always on,” he clarified. “It represents Logan’s canon mutant super senses and elite tracking ability. It only is there when he’s tracking a specific scent / sound (a person, whisky, or another clue scent) - story/mission moments or when he catches whiff of a collectible.” Referencing previous discourse about Final Fantasy’s yellow paint guides , some have said Logan's scent trails remove any potential skill required for chase sequences and any joy of discovery in exploration. Then, earlier this week, Insomniac said it was planning to “further refine the player experience” based on feedback , while insisting it’s “incredibly proud” of the game. Most took that to mean it intended to tweak the “fart gas,” and so it has proved. The patch notes, posted to Insomniac’s website , confirms the hotfix “adjusts the presentation of the Scent Trails and Audio Sense indicators, including reduced opacity to make these visuals less intense.” So, the “fart gas” will feel less in your face from now on. But there’s more. Insomniac said it’s exploring adding toggleable options for a future update, which suggests players may eventually be able to turn off Scent Trails completely. Patch notes are below. Marvel’s Wolverine update v.01.001.005 patch notes: This hotfix addresses some common crashes experienced by a small percentage of players since launch. Additionally, this hotfix adjusts the presentation of the Scent Trails and Audio Sense indicators, including reduced opacity to make these visuals less intense.
